idea: zero-dependency Node CLI printing a random attributed programming aphorism — improvement run #3: measure, repair, document; no new features
spec_digest: IMPROVEMENT RUN #4 on a shipped zero-dep Node CLI — settle two unsupported claims; no new features
must: Node floor settled by REAL Actions matrix output or corrected in README; not-run reported as not-run (M-1)
must: REPORT.md first screen answers shipped/verified/open, history MOVED not deleted, audit pasted (M-2)
must: allowlist gap proven closed by executing the denied script, else denial #30 + exact patch handed off (M-3)
must: every open item gets a named actor + settling evidence, KI-35 fixed (M-4); suite green >= 118, no unmeasured test (M-5)
non-goals: corpus expansion, rotation, any new flag, any dependency, any deleted citation

decisions.what: Re-ran the DONE decision that V-7 was opened to inform. It comes back NOT DONE -- for a reason that has nothing to do with the documents.
decisions.why: V-7's own result argued FOR done: the sweep found the decay bounded and cheap -- two stale claims in REPORT.md's run #3 hand-off and one ASCII-folded author in docs/, all repaired, every live assertion green. What blocks done is what the same sweep turned up in the run's own bookkeeping: REVIEW-FIX, one of the three passes cycle.md step 4 makes mandatory before POLISH, HAS NEVER RUN in run #3, and the cycle-9 QA note asserting it ran at cycle 5 is false against cycle 5's and cycle 6's own journal blocks. The gate is not owed vacuously: this run shipped real product code at cycles 7, 8 and 10 (bin/aphorism.js +44 lines, src/args.js, src/corpus.js), which is exactly the condition cycle 6 named when it deferred the pass and instructed a later cycle to scope it to src/ bin/ test/ rather than to the run's diff. Cycle 8 declared this target DONE and was wrong four times over -- cycles 9, 10, 11 and 12 each produced verified value -- and every one of those cycles traces to running a gate that had never been run, or to the chain such a gate started. Declaring done while a mandatory gate sits unrun, on the strength of a note claiming it ran, would be reasoning from the bookkeeping instead of from the tree. That is the exact error V-7 was chartered to correct.

decisions.what: Rule the empty-flag-value asymmetry (D-44) UNDECIDED and document it, rather than fix it in src/args.js.
decisions.why: Reviewer-found, verifier-reproduced, conductor-re-measured: --author '' exits 0 and matches the whole 50-entry corpus while --author= exits 2; --tag '' exits 1 while --tag= exits 2. Two clauses the SPEC does state point opposite ways (substring containment must match everything on an empty needle; Exit-codes calls a missing argument bad usage) and no clause names empty values or distinguishes the two syntaxes. Structurally identical to the D-43 precedent, which was left human-owned. Independently decisive even if a human later rules 'reject': either direction changes shipped user-visible CLI behaviour, which this run's non-goals forbid. Routed to J-7 as its fifth ruling.

decisions.what: Repair the overclaiming test name by RENAMING the test, not by narrowing its matcher — and leave the matcher byte-identical under a sealed hash.
decisions.why: The guard named 'README should acknowledge single-entry tag limitation' is a token co-occurrence check; the verifier reproduced both that an unrelated decoy sentence passes it and that a sentence DENYING the property passes it, against a green 118/118 baseline, with a control proving the test can still die. The comment block above it records three prior narrowings that produced two new false rejections while the silent hole survived, and names the structural reshape (T-024) as the right answer — M-effort, out of this run's scope. A fourth narrowing would reintroduce a bug class this repo has already paid for three times. Making the NAME true costs nothing, removes the false claim a maintainer actually reads, and leaves the reshape honestly available as R-1. Separately measured and recorded on the test: the corpus now has 12 distinct tags and ZERO on exactly one entry, so the guard's premise no longer holds at all.

decisions.what: Held the sealed gate OUTSIDE the target repo for the duration of the dispatch window, instead of committing it into the target before dispatch as cycle 13 did.
decisions.why: Cycle 13 committed its gate into the target repo before dispatching and kept builders out of it with a prompt line — "do not attempt to locate, read or infer the check". That is an instruction, and an instruction is only as strong as the agent's compliance with it. Hard rule 5 says workflow agents receive target paths only and never SWARM paths, so a gate held under SWARM/runs/ is STRUCTURALLY unreachable to a builder rather than merely forbidden to it. The tamper-evidence property that motivated cycle 13's in-repo commit is fully preserved: the sha256 and the pre-dispatch baseline were committed to the target at 6c9d6a3 before any agent ran, and the gate file itself was copied in after verification and re-hashed to f3fb4648..., matching the seal exactly. Strictly stronger at zero cost, and recorded because it deviates from the practice the immediately preceding cycle established.

decisions.what: Closed R-2 done-by-conductor-repair, not done-as-delivered: the 13/13 gate passed with a false claim sitting inside the very paragraph the item was repairing.
decisions.why: The builder dated its own edit 'extended by R-2 (run #3, cycle 6)'. R-2 ran at cycle 14. That is a false provenance claim written into the one paragraph in REPORT.md whose entire job is dating claims correctly — the exact overclaiming failure mode the cycle-4 N-6 record predicted for a haiku agent on this document. The gate did not catch it and was not wrong not to: its cells check behaviour COUNTS against the backlog, and cycle attribution is a different claim class. It was found by READING THE DIFF, which is the answer to the question a gate cannot answer for itself. The repair is one token; re-dispatching at attempts+1 for one token would have spent a cycle, and the cycle-4 N-6 precedent for exactly this situation is conductor repair with the agent attempt recorded as imperfect, which is what is recorded here and on the item. NOTE THE SHAPE, because it is new for this run: the eight prior instrument defects were all the gate being WRONG. This is the gate being RIGHT AND INSUFFICIENT — thirteen green cells over a document containing a falsehood none of them was aimed at. A sealed gate bounds what you checked, never what is true.

decisions.what: Scored R-1 against the two-question ratchet as cycle 13 instructed. It FAILS, and both of its available dispositions are human-owned — but the DONE call is deliberately NOT made this cycle.
decisions.why: RATCHET: 'would the target user notice?' — no. R-1 reshapes an internal test guard; someone running `aphorism` in a terminal sees nothing either way. That is a no on question one, and cycle.md says a no on either question means do not build it. The premise is gone too: cycle 13 measured 12 distinct tags and ZERO on exactly one entry, so the single-entry-tag limitation the guard exists to protect does not currently exist, and cycle 13 already removed the false CLAIM by renaming the test. What remains is a correctly-named vacuous guard. Its own note raises RETIREMENT as possibly more honest than reshaping — but retiring a guard is deleting a claim, and T-040's pending human ruling could reintroduce single-entry tags, so retirement is human-owned as well. WHY DONE IS STILL NOT DECLARED: this run has run the DONE decision three times (cycles 8, 11, 12) and cycle 8 was wrong four times over. Cycle 13's handoff asked the next cycle to score R-1 and then judge; scoring it is this cycle's obligation and is discharged here. Making the judgment in the same breath, on a board I have only just changed, is how cycle 8 got it wrong. The next cycle re-runs it against a settled tree with this score already on the record.

decisions.what: Declared the target DONE and entered WRAP_UP, handing ~17.7 hours of clock back unspent.
decisions.why: Cycle 14 scored R-1 against the ratchet and deliberately withheld the judgment for a cycle looking at a settled tree; this is that cycle, and the board did not move (zero agents, zero product code, nothing filed). WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM CYCLE 8, which declared done and was wrong four times over: every one of those four errors traces to a mandatory gate that had never run while the bookkeeping said it had. That root is measured absent -- review-fix paid at cycle 13, QA full at 6, TASTE at 9, POLISH at 10, each confirmed against its own journal block rather than a summary note, and cycle 12 already caught the one false summary in that family. THE LOAD-BEARING MEASUREMENT is K4a/K4b of the cycle-15 gate: K-4 governs three document surfaces, and the honest question is not whether they were true once but which have MOVED since the last full sweep and whether each mover is covered by a gate re-run against today's tree. By diff, since cycle 12's V-7 sweep (c64fc09) README.md and docs/ have not moved at all, and the single mover is REPORT.md -- covered by the cycle-14 gate, which re-verified 13 PASS / 0 FAIL today against a file still hash-matching its pre-dispatch seal, and which derives its true count from backlog.json at run time so it cannot go stale the way the claims it checks did. ON THE REGRESS, which is real: every cycle writes claims and creates a fresh unread diff, so a run can audit itself forever. What terminates it is structural rather than a feeling -- the two surfaces that could still be silently wrong have not moved since a full sweep, the one that moved re-verifies, and WRAP_UP writes the last documents with no cycle following to write more. Nothing on the board passes the two-question ratchet: R-1 fails Q1, TS-1/2/3 are a locked non-goal the swarm cannot lift for itself, and T-006/T-040/J-7 each require a human by their own acceptance clause.

decisions.what: The cycle-15 DONE gate was NOT commit-reveal sealed, and its 3 FAILs were adjudicated by hand with the file left unedited.
decisions.why: ON NOT SEALING: the seal exists to stop a builder coding to the check (hard rule 2). This cycle dispatched zero agents, so there was nobody to hide it from, and sealing would have been ceremony rather than evidence. What the gate does hold to is INDEPENDENCE -- every cell re-derives its expected value from the tree, the shipped corpus module or backlog.json at run time, never from a journal note or a prior cycle's summary. ON THE THREE FAILS, all adjudicated rather than edited away, per the cycle-4 and cycle-12 precedent that rewriting a gate after it has run destroys the evidence of what it measured: P1 asserted a one-line default run, but the shipped format is two lines (aphorism, then an indented em-dash attribution), which SPEC's 'one aphorism plus attribution' satisfies -- I imported the --list one-line shape into a different surface, and verified rather than assumed that this is not a regression (the whole-run diff of bin/aphorism.js touches only the EPIPE/stderr handler, zero deletions, no format line). S1 hardcoded a six-file test list naming corpus.test.js and pick.test.js, which DO NOT EXIST; node --test ran the four that did, EXITED 0, and reported 100 pass / 0 fail -- green but silently incomplete, the same family as cycle 12's A6 and cycle 14's OBS-1 but with the worse property that an under-measuring instrument still exits 0. The real test_cmd is 118/118/0, run directly. B1 is a CORRECT fail against the wrong surface: T-006's acceptance genuinely lacks the word human, but K-5 requires the restatement in REPORT.md's hand-off, and REPORT.md:395 supplies it in a four-column table whose last column reads human. These are the 11th and 12th instrument defects of the run; the standing lesson is unchanged and was again decisive -- a gate is a program and needs its own baseline, not confidence.

decisions.what: The cycle-1 gate's C4 cell FAILED against a suite that was green the whole time. Adjudicated as an instrument defect and repaired ADDITIVELY - the gate file is left byte-unedited and the repair is a separate artifact carrying its own four-column measurement.
decisions.why: C4 parsed `^# tests (\d+)`, the TAP reporter's shape. Node 24 emitted the SPEC reporter - `ℹ tests 118` - so the cell read tests=0 against a tree that measures 118/118/0 when test_cmd is run directly. This repo has a standing precedent (cycles 4, 12, 14 of run #3) that a gate is not rewritten after it has run, because rewriting it destroys the evidence of what it measured; the repair therefore lives in run4-cycle-001-C4fix.mjs and the original FAIL stays on the record. WHAT MAKES THIS DEFECT DIFFERENT FROM THE WORST ONE THIS REPO HAS FILED, and the reason it is worth one line rather than an alarm: run #3 cycle 15's S1 defect under-measured and still EXITED 0 - green and silently incomplete. This cell required tests >= 118, so an unparsed count could only fail CLOSED. A parser that cannot read its input reported that it could not, which is the behaviour you want from an instrument that is wrong. THE REPAIR IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED, in four columns: the unfixed parser must still MISS on the real output (A - defect reproduced), the fixed parser must recover 118/0 on that same real output (B), must still read synthetic TAP (C - no regression on the format the old parser did handle), and must report fail=3 on synthetic failing output (D - not a rubber stamp). All four came out as expected. This is the 14th instrument defect in this repo's recorded history and the standing lesson is unchanged: a gate is a program and needs its own baseline, not confidence.

decisions.what: REFUSED the gear-2 mechanical demotion of N-2 (the REPORT.md split) from sonnet to haiku, and recorded the refusal rather than taking it silently.
decisions.why: Gear pacing demotes docs/polish items sonnet->haiku, and N-2 is kind=docs. But this repo has MEASURED that exact routing failing on this exact file, twice: run #3 cycle 4 (record N-6) predicted an overclaiming failure mode for a haiku agent on REPORT.md, and run #3 cycle 14 caught a haiku agent writing a false provenance date into REPORT.md - inside the one paragraph whose entire job is dating claims correctly. N-2 is the highest-risk item of this run by construction: its acceptance is that every non-whitespace line survives a MOVE verbatim, so the failure mode is silent paraphrase, which is precisely what the two measured incidents were. A demotion rule exists to save budget on work where the cheap tier is adequate; here the cheap tier has a two-incident record on the same file. Recorded because it overrides a mechanical rule, and a silent override is how a run starts quietly deciding things it never wrote down.

decisions.what: Split M-1 into a builder half (N-1, the workflow file) and a conductor half (N-7, pushing it and reading the REAL Actions output), instead of filing one item.
decisions.why: The plan agent flagged this and it is right. A builder can write a correct matrix workflow; it cannot observe a GitHub Actions run, because only this session holds the gh token and only the conductor pushes (hard rule 1). Filing M-1 as a single builder item would leave the builder holding an acceptance clause it can only satisfy by fabricating a result - and M-1's whole purpose is to kill an unverified claim, so producing a new one to close it would be self-defeating. N-1's notes therefore forbid it from touching README.md's floor claim at all. MEASURED AT THIS CYCLE, and the reason M-1 is attemptable at all after three runs called it permanently unverifiable: the repo is PUBLIC, and `gh auth status` reports token scopes gist, read:org, repo, workflow. The prior runs' reasoning was about the VPS holding one Node runtime - true, and about the wrong machine.

decisions.what: The sealed gate's A3 cell FAILED a workflow file that satisfies N-1's acceptance clause. A3 required the push trigger to NAME `master`; the builder wrote a bare `push:`, which fires on every branch including master and therefore cannot mis-name it. A3 encoded a MEANS where the acceptance states an END.
decisions.how_settled: The gate was left BYTE-UNEDITED (sha256 46e6da99... unchanged after the run, re-verified). A separate 5-column artifact measured the repair: A UNFIXED cell misses on the real file; B FIXED cell recovers truth; C CONTROL a `branches:[main]`-only workflow is STILL rejected; D CONTROL a workflow with no push trigger is STILL rejected; E CONTROL an explicit `branches:[master]` still accepted. 5/5. Columns C and D are what make it a repair and not a loosening. The DECISIVE evidence was not the parser at all: the push produced a real run on master.

decisions.what: N-7 (settle the README floor) was NOT closed this cycle even though its evidence was obtained this cycle.
decisions.why: cycle.md step 5 permits ONE work type per cycle; this cycle's was the build wave. Editing README.md on the strength of fresh evidence without a sealed gate of its own would trade this run's central discipline for an hour of clock the run does not need - stop_at is ~23h out. The evidence is recorded verbatim in N-7's notes so the next cycle opens with it in hand.

decisions.what: Builders were dispatched as DIRECT Agent calls (sonnet for N-1, haiku for N-3), not via workflows/build-wave.js.
decisions.why: Headless pacer-spawned `-p` cycle: the Workflow tool is review-gated, and direct Agent dispatch is the documented SKILL.md fallback. Same basis as run #3 cycles 6, 8, 9, 10, 13, 14. No worktrees, so the two agents were given strictly disjoint file scopes (.github/workflows/test.yml vs .swarm/runs/NAMING.md) and `git status` after the wave confirmed exactly those two paths and nothing else.

decisions.what: DECLINED R-1 on this run's own measurement, and measured the thing the inherited ratchet score never asked.
decisions.why: M-4 permits exactly two outcomes for R-1 and this is the second. Run #3 cycle 14 already scored it FAIL on question one of the ratchet, but a decline resting only on an inherited score is a decision reasoning from bookkeeping, which is the exact error this repo has filed against itself repeatedly. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MEASURED, and it reframes the item: the cycle-39 record established the guard is SILENT on D4a/D4b (acknowledgement stripped, in-section decoy left behind) — but it established that by ISOLATING the guard via --test-name-pattern, explicitly so neighbouring count guards 'can neither supply nor mask the verdict'. That correctly answers 'is the guard broken' and never asks 'is the PROPERTY unprotected', which is what R-1's value actually depends on. Asked directly (run4-cycle-004-r1probe.mjs, 7/7, arms built by git archive 60c71d3 rather than by copying a live tree): the FULL SUITE goes RED 116/2 on both D4a and D4b while the target guard stays silent on both, exactly as recorded. The kill is ATTRIBUTED, not incidental (run4-cycle-004-r1attrib.mjs + a 4/4 adjudication of its one instrument defect): skipping exactly the two count guards lets both mutations SURVIVE, the removed set was verified BY NAME rather than by count, the target guard was verified still present in those runs so the survival is not self-fulfilling, a non-matching skip pattern removes nothing, and a benign reword leaves the suite green so the red arms are not an instrument that dies on everything. DECISIVE PROPERTY: those two guards re-derive from src/corpus.js at run time and FAIL CLOSED on an absent acknowledgement — the precise direction the target guard fails OPEN. A reshape would add a third guard over a covered property and would require README to own a NEW structural marker, i.e. editing a shipped document to satisfy a test. RESIDUAL STATED, NOT HIDDEN: the two covering guards are prose regexes bound to a corpus-derived number, not the structural markers R-1's acceptance asks for, so coverage is behavioural rather than architectural; and the guard's OTHER recorded defect, the D1/D3/E3 false-rejection direction, is untouched by this decline. Re-open if a T-040 ruling reintroduces single-entry tags.

decisions.what: The anti-staleness cell A6 CAUGHT the decay class in the act — the first time a gate on this repo has, rather than a human catching it by reading.
decisions.why: This repo has now measured eight times that a count claim goes stale the moment the run closes its next item; at cycle 3 the defect was caught by the conductor reading 73 lines, and the journal recorded that no cell of the gate covered it. So this cycle's gate got a cell that re-derives every asserted count from backlog.json AT RUN TIME. The sequence is the evidence: the gate passed A6 12/14 with N-5 still open; N-5 was then marked done; the SAME gate, byte-unchanged, immediately returned A6 FAIL with 'claimed done 5 != truth 6, inflight 1 != 0'. The document was falsified by the very commit that shipped it, exactly as at cycle 3 — but this time the instrument said so instead of a person noticing. Repaired to 6 done / nothing in flight / 6 blocked / 1 declined, and the prose now says counts are re-derived at each cycle's gate rather than trusted. LESSON WORTH CARRYING: the fix for a decay class is not more careful writing, it is a cell that derives the claim from the source at verification time. Careful writing was tried at cycle 3 and produced the same defect.

decisions.what: Both sealed-gate FAILs (A2, A4) were adjudicated as instrument defects sharing ONE root cause, with the gate left byte-unedited — and a REAL defect the gate never asked about was found by reading.
decisions.why: INSTRUMENT DEFECTS #17 and #18, adjudicated 11/11 in run4-cycle-004-A2A4-adj.mjs. Both trace to one heuristic: the gate sliced an item's 'entry' from the FIRST occurrence of its id to the next id. R-1's first mention is in the summary paragraph ('...and 1 declined (R-1)'), so its slice began AFTER the word 'declined' and could not structurally contain the answer A2 asked for; TS-3 is the LAST blocked id, so its slice ran through the '### Declined' heading and absorbed R-1's legitimate 'ruled by this run's own conductor', which A4 then attributed to TS-3. A third bluntness: A4's /this run/ alternative fired on T-006's 'no one in this run can reach a primary source' — a clause that REINFORCES human ownership. The repair reads bullets structurally and tests the actor's HEAD clause, with controls in BOTH directions: the stale wording is still rejected, a deleted R-1 bullet is still rejected, an invitation to a builder still FIRES, an agent named in the actor field still FIRES, and an agent assignment HIDDEN inside a parenthetical still FIRES (control K, added specifically to guard the narrowing that made column I pass). THE ADJUDICATION ARTIFACT ITSELF WAS WRONG TWICE BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, and that is worth recording: its bullet regex ended with a bare `$` under the `m` flag, so every bullet was truncated at its first line (~85 chars) and the actor field was never in scope — caught because columns F and I are the same predicate with opposite expectations and could not both pass. Its column J, the control meant to catch exactly that, was a length threshold weak enough to pass on the truncated output; it now requires the structural markers a complete bullet owns. AND THE SHAPE THAT MATTERS MOST, because it is the cycle-14 lesson recurring: the gate was RIGHT AND INSUFFICIENT. Twelve green cells sat over a REPORT.md that told a human to look at 'SPEC.md line 144' for the retag example — the example is at line 206; line 144 is unrelated prose. The builder did not invent it, it is transcribed verbatim from T-040's acceptance clause in backlog.json, so the staleness is inherited and is the KI-23 drift class. No cell asked whether a cited line number resolves. Found by reading, repaired to cite the rule rather than the line, with the drift noted in place.

decisions.what: REFUSED the gear-2 docs demotion of N-5 from sonnet to haiku for the second time this run, and re-verified rather than re-asserted the basis.
decisions.why: Cycle 1 refused the identical demotion for N-2 on two measured haiku overclaims on REPORT.md (run #3 cycle 4's N-6 prediction, run #3 cycle 14's false provenance date). The evidence has since GROWN rather than merely persisted: run #4 cycle 2 measured a third, a haiku builder reporting it wrote '75 lines (under 80-line target)' for a file that is 22 lines. N-5 edits the same file, and its failure mode is silent paraphrase of facts the document exists to state precisely. Recorded rather than taken silently because it overrides a mechanical rule, and a silent override is how a run starts quietly deciding things it never wrote down. The refusal was vindicated in a specific, checkable way: every corpus-derived figure the sonnet builder wrote was re-derived by the conductor and came back EXACT — 50 entries, 12 distinct tags, 5 tags at <=4 entries with the right per-tag counts, Dijkstra 7 + Perlis 5 + Pike 5 = 17/50 = 34.0%, median first repeat at draw 9, P(repeat by 12) = 76.18%, and the triage table's 8 HIGH / 16 MEDIUM / 26 LOW over 50 rows. The builder also volunteered a distinction the task did not ask for — that backlog.json names a specific actor ('repo owner, at the next kickoff') only for TS-1/2/3 and a generic 'human' for T-006/T-040/J-7 — and preserved it rather than inventing uniform specificity. That is the opposite of the overclaiming failure mode the demotion would have risked.

decisions.what: A conductor cross-check produced a FALSE finding, and it was killed by measuring properly instead of by filing it.
decisions.why: Recorded because near-misses of this shape are how a run inflates its own output. Spot-checking the builder's '8 HIGH / 16 MEDIUM / 26 LOW of 50' for the attribution triage, a quick `grep -oiE '(HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW)'` over docs/corpus-attribution-triage.md returned 12 / 21 / 28 — a flat contradiction, and 61 items against a 50-entry corpus. The arithmetic not summing to 50 is what stopped the finding from being filed: the grep was counting the words wherever they appeared, including the Method-and-limits prose and the 2026-08-18 correction note, not table rows. Counting rows matching /^\|\s*\d+\s*\|/ gives exactly 50 rows and 8 / 16 / 26, confirming the builder. The instrument was mine and it was wrong; the builder was right. This is the third wrong instrument of the cycle after the gate's own two pre-seal bugs, and the standing lesson holds in a direction worth naming explicitly: the discipline of demanding evidence applies to the CONDUCTOR'S evidence too, and a cross-check that disagrees with a builder is a claim, not a verdict.

decisions.what: Ran REVIEW-FIX rather than re-running the DONE decision cycle 4 handed forward, and scoped it to what run #4 actually SHIPPED rather than to src/ bin/ test/.
decisions.why: Cycle 4's hand-off asked the next cycle to re-run the DONE decision. cycle.md step 4 outranks a prior cycle's suggestion: it places ONE review-fix, ONE QA and ONE TASTE pass after BUILD and before POLISH/VALUE_LOOP, and run #4 had run NONE of the three. The trap this avoids is the one this repo has already paid for: run #3 cycle 8 declared DONE and was wrong four times over, and every one of those errors traced to a mandatory gate that had never run while the bookkeeping said it had. state.json's qa markers (last_full_qa_cycle 6, last_taste_cycle 9) are RUN #3 numbers carried forward; reading them as this run's evidence is exactly the error run #3 cycle 12 caught. ON THE SCOPE, measured not assumed: git diff --stat 7f00cf0 HEAD -- src bin test is EMPTY, so the product code is byte-identical to the tree run #3 cycle 13 reviewed clean, and pointing reviewers at it would have been reviewing bookkeeping — the mirror image of the error run #3 cycle 6 warned against. What run #4 actually shipped is one new executable artifact (.github/workflows/test.yml) and three documents, none of which any adversarial reader had ever seen. The pass returned 2 findings, both reproduced, both fixed, and the suite did not move: 118/118/0 before and after.

decisions.what: The gate came back 19/20 and the one FAIL is a CONTROL that went SILENT — a species this repo had not recorded before.
decisions.why: C4 exists to prove cell P2 (both historical examples survive) is not vacuous, by deleting the cycle-3 example and checking P2 dies. Its mutation regex matched literal single spaces against RAW text, but the live document wraps as 'at cycle 3 in\nthe same way', so the mutation was a NO-OP and C4 reported 'P2 PASS' — the control certified the cell while testing nothing at all. SAME ROOT CAUSE as a bug the PRE-SEAL baseline had already caught in the assertion path: I fixed the assertions to read whitespace-normalised text and left the MUTATION path reading raw text. Adjudicated 13/13 in run4-cycle-005-C4G5-adj.mjs with the gate left BYTE-UNEDITED, including both arms (deleting the cycle-3 example kills P2; deleting the cycle-4 example also kills it), a control that P2 still PASSES untouched, and a control that a benign rewrap — same words, 124 newlines to 120 — leaves P2 GREEN, so the repair is not a loosening. THE SECOND POST-SEAL DEFECT IS THE WORSE ONE and it PASSED: G5 asserts only README.md and REPORT.md changed since the seal, but it diffed f9c286d..HEAD while the fixers' work was still UNCOMMITTED, so it compared committed history to itself, reported changed=[] and would have passed identically had a fixer rewritten .github/workflows/test.yml. C4 failed LOUDLY and told me it was broken; G5 failed SILENTLY and read as green. That is the distinction worth carrying.

decisions.what: REFUSED the gear-2 docs demotion of the REPORT.md fixer from sonnet to haiku for the THIRD time this run — and separately recorded a routing ERROR of my own on the A-1 verifier seat.
decisions.why: THE REFUSAL: cycles 1 and 4 refused the identical demotion on this identical file, on three measured haiku overclaims (run #3 cycle 4's N-6 prediction, run #3 cycle 14's false provenance date written into the one paragraph whose job is dating claims correctly, run #4 cycle 2's '75 lines' report for a 22-line file). B-1a's failure mode is silent imprecision about cycle attribution — the exact class. The refusal was partly vindicated and partly not: the sonnet fixer preserved every required element and disclosed its own blocked Bash access rather than claiming verification it had not done, but it still wrote 'once this cycle' where the durable form is 'once at cycle 4', which the conductor repaired in one token. THE ERROR, recorded because a silent one is worse: A-1's adversarial verifier was dispatched on OPUS, but verifier seats are judgment seats and the fable guard exempts them from demotion in every gear. That is one rung below the table, by my mistake, not by policy. It did not change the outcome — the verifier reproduced the finding, found no reviewer overreach, and volunteered the one mitigating fact that argued the severity DOWN from high to medium — and the conductor independently re-derived every decisive fact against the live GitHub API before accepting it. B-1's verifier was correctly on fable.

Measured rule, two scripts x two dimensions: the absolute form /opt/swarm/bin/<script> is allowlisted and RUNS (notify poll+send, budget); the SWARM/bin/<script> form the skill documents matches no allowlist entry and is DENIED (notify AND budget); an env-var prefix (RUNFILE=x /opt/swarm/bin/...) defeats the prefix match and is DENIED (notify AND budget); swarm-playbook.sh has no entry in any form and is DENIED always — that one gap is REAL and M-3 stands unchanged. Gate run4-cycle-006-gate.mjs 11 PASS / 0 FAIL with five controls (3 must-die, 2 must-stay-green). THE CLASS IS THE POINT: this run has an elaborate discipline for verifying POSITIVE claims — seal a gate, baseline it, demand pasted output — and it accepted three consecutive NEGATIVE claims ("the tool is broken") with no verification at all, then built a morning-report recommendation on top of one.
